solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restrain light blow

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a quick slap with the open hand

explanation.surface: Holding someone back with nothing more than a gentle smack.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to put handcuffs on; as a noun it is a light open-handed strike.

clue.text: Hastily seize the sauce

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to snatch up quickly
second meaning: a variant spelling of ketchup

explanation.surface: Someone grabs the bottle of sauce in a hurry at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The run-together spelling is an old variant of ketchup, the tomato sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something up is to snatch it hastily, and catchup is a recognised alternative spelling of ketchup.

clue.text: Fair rental, I conceded, is different, not identical

indicators.note: to be made different is to be changed, so the remaining letters are put in another order
what is conceded is given up, so the letter named before it is surrendered from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be given up

explanation.surface: A landlord conceding a point about a fair rent sounds like a tenancy dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from FAIR RENTAL to leave FARRENTAL, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal twins come from two separate eggs, so they are different rather than identical, unlike monozygotic twins.

clue.text: Probes without warning place threats on board

parts.note: a spot is a place
in chess a check is a threat to the king on the board

explanation.surface: Surprise inspections might find menacing messages pinned to a notice board.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot checks are random unannounced inspections, which is what probes without warning are.

clue.text: Fruit pulp always first class

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food or pulp
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
A is the top grade, first class

explanation.surface: A boast that fruit pulp is invariably top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: AY meaning 'ever, always' is a poetic and Scots word that crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a tropical fruit, also called pawpaw, with orange flesh.

clue.text: Hypocrite begins meal, unpacked from cases

indicators.note: taking contents out of their cases leaves the insides, so each word loses its outermost letters

parts.note: begins is STARTS; its inside, without its cases, is kept
a buffet is a meal; its inside, without its cases, is kept

explanation.surface: A two-faced diner starts eating a meal after unwrapping it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tartuffe is the religious hypocrite of Molière's comedy, whose name became a byword.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière's title character is a sanctimonious fraud, so his name is used for any hypocrite.

clue.text: Once was joining a revolution, now am more sophisticated

parts.note: a phrase for what was so in the past
taken as written
a round is one complete turn or circuit

explanation.surface: Someone who joined a revolution once now considers themself worldly-wise.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been around is an idiom for being experienced in the ways of the world, so I am more sophisticated now.

clue.text: Pyramid builder short of energy food

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Cheops was the pharaoh credited with the Great Pyramid of Giza
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pyramid builder runs out of energy for want of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chops are cuts of meat such as lamb or pork, a common item of food.

clue.text: Slide woman under narrow opening

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means coming after, so the pieces are stacked in that order

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman wriggles through a narrow gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide or slip along smoothly, often with a twisting motion.

clue.text: In the boozer these, drunk, chatter idly

indicators.note: a drunk is all over the place, so the words before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinkers in a pub having a good natter over their pints.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot the breeze is an informal idiom for chatting idly about nothing in particular.

clue.text: Jump onto seat after ordering drink here

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters of the word beside it are reshuffled
one thing landing onto another means it goes on after it

parts.note: seat with its letters reordered
a hop is a small jump

explanation.surface: Someone leaps into a chair once they have ordered a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a café where one goes to have a cup of tea, the drink of the definition.

clue.text: Run a fiddle, taking a little off small cases of meat perhaps

indicators.note: trimming a little from a word removes its final letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
taken as written
a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: A scam that involves skimming a small amount from the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run a fiddle' reads as operating a swindle, but fiddle is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are little pasta parcels typically stuffed with meat, so cases of meat is a fair description with 'perhaps' covering other fillings.

clue.text: Painter in boys' home tangled with urchins

indicators.note: a tangle is a jumble, so the letters of these words are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist in a children's home gets into trouble with the street kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was the Netherlandish painter of the crowded, nightmarish Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: I catch parent outside nurseries

indicators.note: a word placed outside goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Someone catching their mother or father outside a nursery school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurseries' suggests children; here it means places where young trees are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineta, plural of pinetum, are plantations where pine trees are grown, so they are tree nurseries in a loose sense.

clue.text: Criminal related to manager?

parts.note: of can mean belonging or relating to
to fend is to manage, so a fender is fancifully one who manages

explanation.surface: A query about whether a crook is a relative of the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense: one who fends for themself manages.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is one who has broken the law, so the noun is a direct synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Long access road at house? Stop being proud?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, the drive leading to a home
second meaning: to hammer a nail fully in so it no longer sticks up

explanation.walkthrough: A nail standing proud sticks up above the surface; driving it home flattens it. 'Proud' looks like vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a verb for forcing something fully in, and as words it also names the private road up to a dwelling.

clue.text: Vicious gaoler is in women's wing

indicators.note: something vicious is wild and violent, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brutal prison warder works in the female wing of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaoler is the British spelling of jailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a harem, the secluded quarters of a palace set aside for women.

clue.text: Showing pale irises we had planted round garden walk

indicators.note: plants set out around something enclose it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the contraction we'd
an alley is a walk or path in a garden

explanation.surface: Gardeners planted irises with pale flowers along a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irises' look like garden flowers but are the parts of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall eye has a whitish or very pale iris, so walleyed describes eyes like that.

clue.text: Pleasure: I'm holding an ace and four kings

definitions.note: names the shared name of the kings

parts.note: will is one's wish or pleasure, as in 'at will'

indicators.note: a word that holds another has it inside

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A card player gleefully reports a hand with an ace and four kings.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-hand surface hides that 'four kings' is the definition: England's kings of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: England has had four kings named William, so the name is shared by all four monarchs.

clue.text: Weapon gives gunners massive support

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a pier is a heavy pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: An artillery unit backs a weapon with heavy support.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword, a weapon for thrusting.

clue.text: Changing sides in allegiance — to them?

definitions.text: Changing sides in allegiance — to them?

indicators.note: swapping sides means one side letter gives way to the other, left for right

parts.note: loyalty is allegiance

explanation.surface: Wondering whether people who switch allegiance owe it to the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left becomes R for right; the whole clue then describes loyalty owed to the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is classically sworn to the monarch, so royal persons are the ones it is owed to.

clue.text: Old car is something between Mercedes and Cortina

indicators.note: only the stretch lying between is wanted, so each name loses the part away from the gap

parts.note: taken as written; only its tail is kept
taken as written; only its head is kept

explanation.surface: A classic car sits somewhere between a Mercedes and a Ford Cortina.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the end of Mercedes and the start of Cortina, skipping the word 'and'. The Cortina, like the answer, was a popular Ford model in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Escort was a family car sold from 1968 to 2004, now an old model.

clue.text: Consider very important what squirrel may do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to value something highly
second meaning, read literally: to put by a large hoard of food

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the idiom describes a squirrel stashing a big supply of nuts for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attach great value to something; literally it pictures stockpiling provisions.

clue.text: Agreed to welcome fine couples

indicators.note: welcoming a guest takes them in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: yes signals agreement
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Pairs who have said yes are happy to greet good guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke joins two animals together, and as a verb yokes means couples or links.

clue.text: Where His Nibs used to take a dip?

definitions.text: Where His Nibs used to take a dip?

parts.words: Where His Nibs used to take a dip?
parts.note: surface reading: a pompous person's former bathing place
setter's reading: the pen nibs that were once dipped in ink at a school desk

explanation.walkthrough: 'His Nibs' is a mocking title for a self-important man; here the nibs are steel pen points.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school desks had a small ink reservoir into which dip pens were dunked for ink.

clue.text: Admit ambition is an embarrassing mistake

parts.note: to own up is to admit
a goal is an aim or ambition

explanation.surface: Confessing one's aspirations can be a cringeworthy blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into your own net is a classic football blunder, and the phrase is now used for any self-inflicted error.

clue.text: Girl maintaining missive from school gives fake news

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold up or keep, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a miss is a girl
a school report is sent home to parents

explanation.surface: A pupil doctors her school report to mislead her parents.
explanation.definitionFit: To misreport is to give an inaccurate account, which is what spreading fake news does.

clue.text: Raise embankment in sound

indicators.note: in sound means what follows is matched by how it is said, not how it is written

parts.note: a levee is a river embankment

explanation.surface: Building up a flood bank in a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be a strait of water; here it signals pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy is to raise a tax or troops, the sense of raise as collect.
